title: Transport theory for a generic two-arm co-propagating Majorana interferometer with Majorana fermion and edge vortex tunneling
authors: Domenico Giuliano, Andrea Nava, Fabian Hassler, Reinhold Egger
abstract: Co-propagating chiral Majorana edge modes are predicted to exist in proximity-coupled quantum anomalous Hall systems. They combine the exciting prospects of edge vortices as flying non-Abelian Ising anyons, with their fully electrical detection through anyon fusion processes. In this setup, electrical transport arises from the interference of a pair of Majorana edge states. By bosonizing the model with an additional replica sector, we generalize previous treatments to fully asymmetric configurations. We analyze a Mach-Zehnder interferometer and show that while the DC conductance does not exhibit signatures of edge-vortex interference, at low frequencies, this interference manifests as an effective capacitance. This quantity is sensitive to the non-Abelian anyon statistics of edge vortices and, in particular, carries signatures of their topological spin and nontrivial conformal dimension. We demonstrate that the thermal length $l_T = \hbar v/(πk_B T)$ is the relevant scale at low temperatures $T$, analogous to quasiparticle transport in conventional quantum Hall edge states with velocity $v$. As long as the interferometer arm lengths match within this length scale, transport signatures of the non-Abelian statistics of edge vortices remain visible.
summary: This work develops a transport theory for a Majorana interferometer incorporating edge vortex tunneling. It finds that while DC conductance is insensitive to topological effects, the low-frequency response reveals an effective capacitance sensitive to the non-Abelian statistics of the edge vortices. This provides a measurable diagnostic for topological physics in superconducting quantum devices.
main_problem: To develop a transport theory for a generic two-arm co-propagating Majorana interferometer that incorporates both Majorana fermion tunneling and the effects of edge vortex (EV) tunneling.
main_result: While the DC conductance does not show signatures of edge-vortex interference, the interference manifests as an effective capacitance at low frequencies, which is sensitive to the non-Abelian anyon statistics of the edge vortices.
method: The theory employs a replicated bosonization field theory framework to analyze the linear-response conductance tensor, generalizing previous treatments to asymmetric configurations.
model_or_system: The system is a Majorana interferometer realized on a Topological Insulator proximitized by a Superconductor, featuring two co-propagating chiral Majorana edge modes and coupling points for both Majorana fermions and EVs.
key_observables: Effective capacitance ($C_{	ext{eff}}$) at low frequencies, and the frequency-dependent conductance tensor $G(\omega)$.
important_parameters: Thermal length $\ell_T = \hbar v / (\pi k_B T)$, and the degree of asymmetry in the interferometer arms ($\delta L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the EV size is negligible compared to the thermal length $\ell_T$, and the theory is generalized to handle arbitrary length mismatches.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic setup of the interferometer, showing the two chiral Majorana modes and tunneling processes involving EVs, and show color-scale plots of the finite-temperature DC conductance dependence on tunneling amplitudes.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the initial Hamiltonian formulation (including Majorana and EV tunneling) to the application of a replicated bosonization framework to calculate the frequency-dependent conductance, distinguishing between DC and AC responses.
why_interesting: The focus on topological signatures (non-Abelian statistics) measurable via capacitance in a superconducting platform makes it highly relevant for understanding topological quantum computation pathways.
